blocks.text: Let's solve this one step by step. Negative four squared, divided by the quantity negative two, squared, plus six times the quantity negative one, cubed.
Exponents first, and watch the signs. Minus four squared has no parentheses, so only the four is squared: that is negative sixteen. Negative two squared is four. Negative one cubed is negative one.
Now division and multiplication. Negative sixteen divided by four is negative four. Six times negative one is negative six.
Negative four plus negative six is negative ten.
So the answer is negative ten.
Watch out for these traps. If you square the negative four, sign and all, you get negative two. If you multiply by three instead of cubing, you get negative twenty-two.
